note: P4364 (Pro 30:9) — lest, full, I deny you; or, poor, I steal and profane the name of my God.

dims.v: self-sufficient forgetting — the satiety that denies God, 'who is the LORD?'
the denying of God in plenty — the danger that satiety breeds self-sufficient forgetting, so that the full man says 'who is the LORD?', needing God no longer in his own eyes
the theft of want it is set against (267322)
set against the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name

kachash (deny/deceive) — 'lest I be FULL and DENY you and say, 'who is the LORD?'' (30:9); prosperity tempts a man to self-sufficient forgetting of God. Agur prays against riches lest plenty make him deny his Maker (cf Deut 8:12-14).
desperation-sin — the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name
the stealing that poverty may drive a man to, profaning the name of his God — the danger that want breeds desperation-sin, dishonouring God by the theft it provokes
the denial of plenty it is set against (267316)
set against the satiety that denies God

ganab (steal) — 'or lest I be poor and STEAL and profane the name of my God' (30:9); poverty too has its spiritual peril, driving a man to theft that shames God. Agur prays against want no less than wealth. Emergent: desperation-sin as the danger of poverty (cf 6:30-31).
